description:
CastelBrando sits on a hilltop above Cison di Valmarino in the Treviso province of Veneto, a medieval castle complex of 10th-century origins that today operates as a luxury hotel and wellness resort. The setting is extraordinary: the castle crowns a steep ridge in the Valmarino valley, surrounded on all sides by the Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Hills — a UNESCO World Heritage landscape of stepped vineyards, rural churches, and vine-covered slopes that forms the appellation for some of Italy's most celebrated Prosecco. From the castle's terraces and pool areas, the Prosecco Hills landscape unfolds in every direction.

For visitors coming to CastelBrando for the day, the draw is the Princess Spa — a wellness facility built directly within the castle's ancient structures. This is not a modern spa that happens to occupy a historic building in a conventional way: the pools run along the medieval walls, using the stone as both architecture and backdrop. The Roman-era hypocaust — an underfloor heating system of the type used in Roman bathhouses — survives within the castle's lower levels and has been incorporated into the spa design rather than set aside as a museum exhibit. The medieval cryptoporticos, vaulted corridors of genuine antiquity, are accessible from the wellness areas. The experience is one of relaxation inside a genuinely ancient building, with the architectural fabric itself — stone walls, vaulted ceilings, Roman structural engineering — present throughout.

Guests who have visited through the GYG day-access product rate the experience 4.9★ across 81 reviews, which places it among the highest-rated wellness experiences of any kind in the Veneto. The reviews consistently single out the pools along the castle walls and the setting within the Prosecco Hills landscape as the defining elements of the visit. This is a wellness experience, not a castle heritage tour; visitors come to relax within a medieval building rather than to learn its history room by room. That said, the architectural fabric — the walls, the cryptoporticos, the hypocaust — is of genuine interest, and the combination of Roman, medieval, and panoramic elements makes the castle one of the more architecturally fascinating spa settings anywhere in northern Italy.

For visitors staying overnight as hotel guests, the experience extends into the evenings: Cison di Valmarino is a beautifully preserved Veneto hill village, the castle grounds offer walking in the Prosecco Hills, and the surrounding DOCG appellation can be explored at leisure by car the following morning before the day-trip visitors arrive.
history:
CastelBrando takes its name from the Brandolini family, who held the hilltop fortification above Cison di Valmarino from the medieval period and built it into a substantial military and residential complex across successive centuries. The origins of the site trace to the 10th century, when control over the Valmarino valley and the mountain passes between the Veneto plain and the Treviso hinterland made a hilltop fortification at this position a strategic necessity. The castle that the Brandolini developed was not a single building but a complex of defensive towers, residential wings, and enclosing walls that accumulated over several generations of investment.

The structural evidence within the site points to an even older occupation. The hypocaust system preserved in the castle's lower levels is a Roman-era construction — an underfloor heating technology associated with Roman baths and heated rooms — suggesting that the hilltop was used or built upon in antiquity before the medieval castle rose above it. The Brandolini builders appear to have incorporated some of these earlier structures into their own construction rather than clearing them away.

The castle passed through various phases of ownership and transformation across the early modern and modern periods, expanding from a purely military fortification into an aristocratic residence of considerable scale. Its conversion into a luxury hotel and spa in the late 20th century was the most recent and most radical transformation — one that preserved the medieval fabric while introducing entirely new functions within the ancient walls, so that the Princess Spa now occupies the spaces where the Roman hypocaust and medieval cryptoporticos survive most legibly.
how_to_visit:
**Getting there:** CastelBrando is in Cison di Valmarino, approximately 45 kilometres north of Treviso and 75 kilometres north of Venice. By car from Treviso, take the SP635 and SP635var toward Conegliano then follow the SP15 to Cison di Valmarino (approximately 1 hour). From Venice, allow approximately 1 hour 15 minutes by car. The castle is well signposted in the village. There is limited public transport to Cison di Valmarino; a car gives the most flexibility for combining the visit with Prosecco winery stops in the valley. Conegliano station, served from Venice (approximately 35 minutes) and Treviso (approximately 20 minutes), is 15 kilometres south; a taxi or rideshare covers the final leg.

**Tickets:** The GYG Princess Spa access (t761906, 4.9★/81 reviews, from €60) covers spa and pool access within the castle complex — including the pools along the medieval walls, the cryptoporticos, and the Roman hypocaust areas. This is a wellness experience, not a castle tour; book in advance, especially on weekends and during the Prosecco harvest season in September and October. Overnight hotel stays are bookable directly at castelbrando.it and extend the experience into the castle grounds and the surrounding Prosecco Hills at dusk and dawn.

**Practical tips:** The outdoor pools along the castle walls are the signature experience and are most spectacular in clear weather, when the Prosecco Hills landscape extends in every direction below the castle. Plan the visit for a day with a good weather forecast if outdoor pool time is a priority. The indoor spa areas — including the hypocaust and cryptoportico sections — are comfortable year-round and are the best option in poor weather. Book at least two days ahead; weekend slots sell out.

**Combine with:** The Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Hills UNESCO landscape (surrounding the castle on all sides) — CastelBrando sits at the heart of the appellation; a visit combining the spa with a Prosecco winery tour in the valley below makes a complete Veneto slow-travel day.

faqs.question: Is CastelBrando a heritage visit or a spa day?
faqs.answer: Primarily a spa day — and that is how it should be booked and approached. The Princess Spa is built within genuine medieval and Roman structures (the castle walls, medieval cryptoporticos, and a Roman hypocaust are all present and integrated into the spa design), so the ancient architecture is very much part of the experience. But CastelBrando does not offer a guided heritage tour of the castle in the conventional sense; visitors come to relax in an extraordinary ancient setting, not to move through curated rooms with explanatory panels. The GYG product (t761906) is a spa and pool access ticket, not a guided castle visit.

faqs.question: What is a hypocaust and why does it matter at CastelBrando?
faqs.answer: A hypocaust is a Roman underfloor heating system — a raised floor supported on pillars that allowed hot air and gases from a furnace to circulate beneath the floor surface, warming the room above. The technology was widely used in Roman bathhouses and heated rooms across the empire. The hypocaust preserved within CastelBrando's lower levels is a rare survival that indicates Roman-era occupation or building on the hilltop before the medieval castle was constructed. What makes it unusual at CastelBrando is that it has been incorporated into the Princess Spa as a living architectural element rather than enclosed as a museum exhibit — visitors experience the structure in context within a contemporary wellness space.

faqs.question: Can I stay overnight at CastelBrando rather than just visiting for the day?
faqs.answer: Yes — CastelBrando operates as a full-service luxury hotel within the castle complex, and overnight stays are the way to experience the site at its best. Hotel guests have access to the castle grounds, the surrounding Prosecco Hills, and the spa facilities across the full day and evening rather than during a bounded day-pass window. Evenings in Cison di Valmarino are very quiet, and the castle's hilltop position means that the Prosecco Hills landscape is visible at dusk and dawn from the hotel rooms and terraces. Book hotel stays directly at castelbrando.it.
